title: TaReD: Tool-Aware Recursive Decomposition for Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.11268v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agents combine reasoning with tools to interact with external systems and complete real-world tasks. Early agents typically interleave reasoning and actions along a single execution chain. On complex tasks, this chain becomes unreliable because growing histories obscure intermediate dependencies and allow early planning errors to propagate. Recursively decomposing a complex task into smaller subtasks offers a natural solution, yet effective decomposition must account for the system's capabilities so that each subtask can be executed by the available tools. In realistic systems, however, tool libraries can be too large to expose in full. Injecting every tool description consumes substantial context while making relevant tools harder to retrieve and useful task boundaries harder to identify. translated_title: TaReD：面向长程任务的工具感知递归分解
translated_abstract: 智能体将推理与工具相结合，与外部系统交互以完成现实世界的任务。早期的智能体通常在单一执行链上交替进行推理与行动。在复杂任务中，这种链条变得不可靠，因为不断增长的历史记录会掩盖中间依赖关系，并使早期的规划错误不断传播。将复杂任务递归分解为较小的子任务是一种自然的解决方案，然而有效的分解必须考虑系统的能力，以确保每个子任务都能由可用的工具执行。但在现实系统中，工具库可能过于庞大而无法完整呈现。注入每个工具的描述会消耗大量上下文，同时使相关工具更难被检索，有用的任务边界也更难被识别。我们提出了工具感知的递归分解方法，它按照功能关系将工具组织成一个能力层次结构。在执行过程中……
tldr: 提出TaReD方法，通过按功能关系将工具组织成能力层次结构，实现工具感知的递归任务分解，从而让智能体在长程复杂任务中更可靠地规划与执行。
en_tdlr: TaReD proposes tool-aware recursive decomposition that organizes tools into a capability hierarchy based on functional relationships, enabling agents to reliably plan and execute long-horizon tasks.
